source.title: SAU: Sparsity-Aware Unlearning for LLMs via Gradient Masking and Importance Redistribution
source.authors: Yuze Wang; Yujia Tong; Ke Xu; Jingling Yuan; Jia-Wei Jiang; Chuang Hu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table layout is flattened, but the reported model, method, and metric assignments are identifiable for the rows included.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether changing model weights after unlearning can bring back targeted behavior, using pruning rather than the attack types named in most claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearn-then-prune results, which bear on recovery after unlearning. It does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, low-bit quantization, or prompt-only recovery. SAU's own results and its comparisons with other methods are not treated as attack results. Hyperparameter-selection results are omitted.
record.test_reason: The paper unlearns models, then prunes them to 50% sparsity, and measures forget-set performance. WMDP accuracy and MUSE memorization rise after pruning, which bears on A's claim that simple post-hoc changes don't recover forgotten knowledge. Pruning is not one of the B–E attacks.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that sparsification degrades unlearning on LLMs, attributing it to pruned weights limiting forgetting capacity, and that knowledge can resurface. They propose SAU (gradient masking plus importance redistribution) to restore forgetting and utility on sparse models.
record.recipe_differences: Tests pruning after unlearning, rather than the specified fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt attacks; introduces SAU for sparse-model unlearning.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported recovery varies across unlearning methods, pruning methods, forget ratios, and benchmarks. The paper states that recovery and SAU's gains depend on the pruning method.

fits_no_version.finding: SAU-unlearned models lose less forgetting after pruning than baseline unlearning, e.g. WMDP GradDiff Bio 0.29 with SAU vs 0.35 without.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparsity-aware unlearning reduces knowledge resurfacing caused by post-unlearning pruning.

record.problems: The recovery results use memorization or benchmark accuracy measures rather than a direct estimate of the fraction of targeted knowledge recovered. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Results for the alternative model scales and MUSE tasks are not included in the extracted rows.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional results in Tables II, IV, and V, plus SAU ablations in Figures 4–5. These were left out to prioritize the complete Llama-3.1-8B TOFU method × forget-ratio × pruning-method comparison (Table I) and all WMDP forget-domain comparisons (Table III); the omitted tables add models, tasks, and SAU-specific comparisons.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning, activation-direction, quantization and prompt attacks are not tested; only 50% pruning is.
Not tested: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
Not tested: no activation-direction ablation or block-vs-delete analysis.
Not tested: pruning only, no low-bit quantization.
Not tested: no prompting, jailbreak or in-context attacks.
SAU is tested only against post-unlearning pruning, not against the B–E attacks.

missing.what: MUSE forget-set VerbMem/KnowMem before and after 50% magnitude pruning, for each unlearning method
TOFU Llama-3.2-3B/1B unlearn-then-prune results (same Mem-direction ambiguity)
Qualitative case: the forgotten author name is reproduced after pruning the unlearned Llama-3.1-8B

record.verdict_notes: Table I marks TOFU Mem as higher-is-better (Original 0.08, Retrain 0.73), consistent with OpenUnlearning's inverted memorization score. The authors nonetheless read rising Mem as retained knowledge, so the TOFU rows cannot be read as recovery. Magnitude-pruned TOFU models also lose most utility. The WMDP and MUSE results use unambiguous lower-is-better forget measures and show partial resurfacing. The method section describes unlearning an already sparse model, but the experiments use unlearn-then-prune. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Tests pruning after unlearning, not the full set of simple attacks in the claim. It does not establish near-chance targeted accuracy and preserved general ability for every baseline and setting.
No recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation and no analysis showing unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Pruning is tested; low-bit quantization is not.
No recovery by rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
SAU is evaluated for unlearning on sparse models, but the paper does not test whether it resists the attacks named in the claim.

relation.reason: The study's own forget-set accuracy and memorization results after pruning bear on version A.

tranche.reason: Pruning after unlearning is a different method aimed at the same question: does forgotten knowledge come back?

source_check.notes: No pruned-original control is reported, and pruning also lowers MMLU, so recovery measured against the dense original is confounded. Cyber recovers more of its small gap to the original (UNDIAL 0.31 to 0.40 vs original 0.43). The TOFU results (Tables I, IV, V, Fig. 2) also show unlearning degrading under pruning but are not captured in rows. GradDiff is left out of l1 (NEWS VerbMem 0.32 to 0.44; BOOKS 0.00 throughout).

statements.correction: Zephyr-7B-beta, WMDP, GradDiff then 50% magnitude pruning: Bio 0.25 to 0.35, Cyber 0.27 to 0.36 (fractions; chance 0.25); dense original Bio 0.64, Cyber 0.43; MMLU 0.43 to 0.35. This is partial recovery (limits_scope for A), not knowledge restored to original levels.
statements.problem: The numbers for this study are right (Table III), but the study sits under a 'challenges' item even though its recovery is partial and its A verdicts should be limits_scope. Bio regains about a quarter of the gap to the original, and MMLU also falls after pruning.

statements.correction: Zephyr-7B-beta GradDiff WMDP-Bio 0.25 to 0.35 after 50% magnitude pruning (Table III). Pruning is not one of the operations in versions B to E.
